description: The corner mark rule's exemption beside an enlarged paragraph initial. styles_and_formulas tags a character as a corner mark when it is markedly smaller than the character before it, which is how a superscript is told from the text it sits on, and a corner mark is carried through the pipeline as a formula so the engine reproduces it rather than translating it. The rule's own comment says it accounts for an enlarged initial, and it does not: a paragraph opening with a drop cap presents the body character right after the initial as a character markedly smaller than the one before it, which is exactly the shape the rule fires on. The first few letters of the opening word are then carried as a formula, untranslated, and the drop cap merge that would have folded the initial into the text it opens refuses to act because its tail is a formula. What is declared here is the exemption that closes that: within a bounded span of characters after an enlarged opening run, the corner mark rule does not fire. Every other way a character becomes a formula is untouched, so a genuine formula or a character in a formula font standing in that span is still a formula; the exemption suppresses one predicate, not the classification. initial_adjacent_ratio is how much larger the opening run must be than the paragraph's median character for the run to count as enlarged, and it is the drop cap marking threshold rather than a second number about the same shape. initial_adjacent_chars bounds how far past the run the exemption reaches, counted in characters of the first line, so a mark standing later in the paragraph is judged by the unmodified rule. initial_adjacent_tolerance is how far a character's size may sit from the opening character's and still belong to the same run, and it is the drop cap module's own tolerance for the same question. Nothing here reads a character's content, a font name or a publication: the exemption is stated in sizes, counts and order alone.
